chose: rebuild the crossing diagram as a MATRIX schematic: one grid row per crossing, regions as vertical bus-bar columns, guard names in one left-aligned column, rows grouped into organ bands
over: the layered box-and-arrow DAG with labels placed greedily in the gutters
canvas (rejected in the brief: costs selectable text, print fidelity, prefers-color-scheme, DOM)
because: the layered DAG could not satisfy the brief simultaneously: uniform node width + even gutters + orthogonal-only routing + reserved lanes that visibly connect + organ clustering. Organs cut ACROSS the region layering (hoist: 6 organs own 14 crossings whose from/to pairs share no region grouping), so any organ bracket over a layered layout is a bounding box over scattered labels. Giving every crossing its OWN row makes organ grouping contiguous by construction, makes every edge a single horizontal run that cannot be obstructed (the four floating rails were layer-skipping bypasses whose risers coincided), and puts all 14 guard names on one vertical alignment line.

chose: delete the scriptless selection layer: the radio group, the per-guard generated CSS, and the absolutely-positioned label hotspots
over: keeping the hotspot overlay and only re-laying-out the SVG under it
because: the overlay pinned the figure to one pixel size (hit rects were computed in SVG user units and emitted as absolute CSS px), so the picture could not scale to the column and every guard name had to be placed where a hit area was rather than where the grid wanted it. The replacement is 60 lines of generic listener that names no symbol — unlike the generated rules it cannot fall out of step with the data — and the page still carries every mark, number and sentence with scripting off. The invariant that mattered (self-containment) is now tested directly: no http(s), src=, @import, fetch(, XHR, WebSocket, import(, link, iframe.

chose: the crossing set of the project this was dogfooded on is 13/14 tier-2 and 12/14 security — the tiers are nearly a constant, so the tier encoding is carrying almost no information on the very project it was designed against
couldBe: the atlas genuinely grades almost everything totality-checked because that is what the codebase is
tier-1 (enshrined) requires a via-guard the atlas can only infer in narrow cases, so the grade is an artifact of what the instrument can see
discriminatedBy: count enshrined crossings across several dogfooded projects; if tier-1 is ~1 everywhere regardless of codebase, it is the instrument, and the diagram should encode something with variance instead

chose: keep :target tabs and checkbox disclosures scriptless even though inline script is now allowed
over: moving tab switching into the same listener that does selection
because: the no-script rule was lifted because it CONSTRAINED THE LAYOUT, and :target constrains nothing — it costs no pixel rect, and it makes a tab a linkable URL, which a click handler would have to re-implement. A test now asserts the script never mentions #map/#journal/#trajectory/display, so the boundary is enforced rather than remembered.

chose: no reserved routing lanes — measured 4 of 14 layer-skipping crossings on the dogfood project, and the row layout makes the concept have zero subjects
over: reserved lanes at fixed grid offsets below the figure, with fanned-out risers so each edge is traceable
because: the brief asked for reserved lanes because the old layout had four bypass edges sharing coincident risers, reading as rails attached to nothing. Query: count crossings where layer(to) != layer(from)+1. With one grid row per crossing EVERY row is its own reserved lane, so a layer-skipping crossing is the same object as any other and its run cannot be obstructed. The mechanism has no subjects; the subtraction does its work.
